chunks: about a man who bought from another man one hundred mann of brass for such-and-such, while the seller did not have what had been bought from him.
So he said: "There is no harm, if he delivers to him the weight that was stipulated upon him."

key_terms.أَبُو الصَّبَّاحِ الْكِنَانِيُّ: the narrator who asked the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.اشْتَرَى: bought; entered into a purchase transaction
key_terms.اشْتُرِطَ: was stipulated; made a contractual condition
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.مِائَةَ مَنٍّ: one hundred mann; a specified measure of weight

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell a specified weight of goods if the seller does not yet possess them at the time of sale?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on a sale involving a specified weight of brass, even when the seller did not possess the goods at the time of the transaction. The ruling permits it so long as the agreed weight is fully delivered. It relates to commercial law and discussions connected to usury and valid sale conditions.
